lessons.heading: # Day 7 — LLMs, Grounding, RAG, and Retrospective
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 7 — LLMs, Grounding and RAG'. Panel1 main flow Question → Retrieve source chunks → Build prompt (question + evidence + instructions) → LLM → Answer with source references. Panel2 offline indexing Documents → chunks → embeddings + metadata → index; index supplies retriever. Label 'Retriever finds evidence; LLM generates text'. Panel3 'Prompting: defines task' / 'Grounding: supplies evidence' / 'Insufficient evidence? Say so'. Panel4 evaluation checklist 'Retrieval: relevant evidence?', 'Generation: supported claims?', 'End-to-end: useful answer?' and caution 'RAG reduces, but does not eliminate hallucinations. Check privacy, bias and stale sources. Treat retrieved text as data, not trusted instructions.' No fake scores.
lessons.title: LLMs, Grounding, RAG, and Retrospective

lessons.heading: # Day 6 — Semantic Search and Retrieval
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 6 — Semantic Search and Retrieval'. Panel1 two-lane flow 'Index once: documents → chunks + metadata → document embeddings → index'; 'Per query: question → query embedding → search index → ranked top-k chunks'. Clearly show index feeds search. Use compatible embedding model for both. Panel2 keyword versus semantic: exact terms useful for IDs; meaning-based matches useful for paraphrases; hybrid combines both. Query 'How do I send it back?' matched to 'Return policy'. Panel3 ranking 'Cosine compares direction, not truth' / 'Top-k is a count, not a confidence threshold' / 'Filter by metadata before or during search'. Panel4 evaluation 'Relevant evidence in top-k?', 'Missing or irrelevant results?', 'Inspect sources and test varied queries'. Footer note 'Retrieval returns source text; generation is a separate step.'
lessons.title: Semantic Search and Retrieval

lessons.heading: # Day 5 — Embeddings and Cosine Similarity
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 5 — Embeddings and Cosine Similarity'. Panel1 Text → embedding model → dense vector. Show 'car' and 'automobile' with nearby arrows labeled 'semantic similarity is model-dependent'. Panel2 sparse vs dense: fixed vocabulary ['car','dog','apple']; text 'car car' → counts [2,0,0]. Dense embedding [0.2,-0.4,0.7,...] 'illustrative learned features; coordinates are not named concepts'. Panel3 cosine equation 'cosine(a,b) = (a · b) / (||a|| × ||b||)' and three geometrically correct arrow pairs: same direction +1, perpendicular0, opposite directions−1. 'For nonzero vectors; compares direction, not magnitude'. Panel4 'High similarity is not probability or truth', 'Opposite direction does NOT necessarily mean antonyms', 'Learned representations can miss context or reflect bias'. No flattening text. No semantic names for axes. No assertion dense vectors cannot contain zeros.
lessons.title: Embeddings and Cosine Similarity

lessons.heading: # Day 4 — Text Classification Workflow
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 4 — Text Classification Workflow'. Main flow Labeled text → split raw text → training pipeline TF-IDF then classifier → predictions on unseen text → evaluate. Training fits vocabulary, IDF and classifier; held-out uses fitted vectorizer transform only then predict. Example ticket 'My package is late' → 'delivery'. Pipeline fits preprocessing inside each training fold in CV. Metrics: precision of predicted positives, recall of actual positives, F1 balance, confusion matrix inspects errors. Check imbalance, duplicates and misclassifications. Never fit TF-IDF on held-out text.
lessons.title: Text Classification Workflow

lessons.heading: # Day 3 — Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 3 — Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF'. Exact vocabulary [good,bad,product] and document 'good product good' → count vector [2,0,1]. Documents become rows, vocabulary terms columns; zero means absent term. TF term frequency within document; DF number of documents containing term; IDF downweights common terms across documents; TF-IDF = TF × IDF before optional vector normalization. Useful for classification and lexical retrieval. Unigram representation ignores word order and can miss synonyms. Fit vocabulary and IDF on training data only.
lessons.title: Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF

lessons.heading: # Day 2 — Text Cleaning, Tokenization, and Vocabulary
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 2 — Tokenization and Text Representation'. Raw text 'Not good!' → task-aware cleanup → tokens ['not','good','!']. Vocabulary IDs PAD0 UNK1 not2 good3 !4; sequence [2,3,4] padded [2,3,4,0,0]. IDs are identifiers, not counts or semantic distances. Tokens may be words, subwords or characters. Sequence length is token count. Preserve negation; punctuation/case can matter; cleaning depends on task.
lessons.title: Text Cleaning, Tokenization, and Vocabulary

lessons.heading: # Day 1 — NLP Framing and Text Basics
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 13 Day 1 — NLP Framing and Text Basics'. Flow raw language → task-aware preparation → numeric representation → model or retrieval → result. Define document one text, corpus collection, tokens pieces, vocabulary known tokens. Three task branches classification returns category, retrieval returns source passages, generation produces new text. Context matters: 'good' versus 'not good', ambiguous 'bank'. Numeric IDs alone do not encode meaning. Evaluate usefulness and errors; consider bias/privacy.
lessons.title: NLP Framing and Text Basics

lessons.heading: # Phase 7 — Final Retrospective and Capstone Write-Up
lessons.prompt: Create a clean high-resolution landscape textbook infographic PNG. PURE WHITE background everywhere, especially behind the navy title. NO gradients, dark backgrounds, shadows, textures or photographic backdrops. Large legible navy sans-serif text, restrained pale teal/blue/amber panels, generous whitespace. Exactly 4 main panels maximum. Meaningful diagrams and precise arrow directions. Use ONLY the specified content; no extra topics or invented claims. Short labels, not paragraphs. Bottom 'Learning overview • Read alongside the lesson'. Title 'Week 12 Phase 7 — Retrospective and Model Defense'. Project flow problem → data → baseline → CNN candidate → validation comparison → selected model → final assessment → reflection. Three evidence questions What happened? Why might it have happened? What next? Important actual lesson finding 'The simpler baseline outperformed the CNN candidate in this experiment.' Do not invent scores or causal explanations. Distinguish observed evidence from hypotheses about architecture optimization data and capacity. Conclude more complex does not mean better; record limitations and next controlled experiment.
